quote: Oh, a lot of years. He lived here since it was built in 1968, of course, that he died.
stewart_read: Customer discloses the death of her husband unprompted, a genuine trust-gift moment per schema. The rep's response moves straight to 'You love your home?' without acknowledging the loss at all.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have registered this as small talk not requiring a stop, given the call's brisk pace throughout — but the schema explicitly flags this category as high-value and low-cost to acknowledge.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to pause 2-3 seconds on any loss/health/financial disclosure with a brief acknowledgment before continuing the verify sequence — costs nothing and builds trust with an anxious, fixed-income customer.

quote: the total bill is around 500 or more, sometimes close to 6.
stewart_read: A large, specific bill figure is captured cleanly, but the rep's very next line pivots to the roof question rather than reflecting the number back or connecting it to the earlier affordability fear.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep could be deliberately deferring the flip to let the specialist do the numbers conversation — but nothing later in the call revisits this figure, undermining that read.
coaching_implication: Show the rep this exact spot: after capturing $500-600/month, a one-line flip ('that's exactly the kind of bill our program is built to bring down') would have tied the fear from 00:21 directly to the appointment.

quote: Well, I do you have a shingle roof?
stewart_read: Minor verbal stumble during the roof question causes brief confusion ('single' vs 'shingle') but is self-corrected quickly and does not derail the call.
coaching_implication: Low priority — flag only if this kind of verbal fumbling recurs across other calls from this rep.

quote: Then you have a credit score over 6 70?
stewart_read: Customer answers 'I don't know' and the rep immediately says 'Okay. We'll just say yes,' waving through a hard qualifier without any real verification.
alternative_hypothesis: This could reflect a floor norm of not hard-DQing on stated uncertainty (per the schema's open policy question on stated-vs-pulled credit) — but the rep doesn't flag it for the closer either, so the ambiguity isn't resolved, just skipped.
coaching_implication: Clarify with the rep whether 'I don't know' should be treated as a soft pass-through to the closer's credit pull, and if so, coach them to say that explicitly rather than silently assuming yes.

quote: Right. And that says my bill is 25.69% higher than last year, the March.
stewart_read: The customer hands the rep a second, sharper anchor than the original bill figure — an unprompted year-over-year increase — and the rep's response is a flat 'Oh,' with no reflection or forward-pull.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have been mid-task helping her navigate the bill portal and simply didn't have bandwidth to also work the emotional angle — plausible given the technical back-and-forth in this stretch, but the moment still went unused.
coaching_implication: Point to this exact line as a missed hook: 'that increase is exactly why the specialist wants to look at your numbers' would have used her own words to build momentum into the appointment.

quote: So we got everything we need. I actually just sent you a appointment. I actually don't know if it's a phone call or in person. Let me just find out real quick. Okay?
stewart_read: The rep hadn't confirmed appointment channel before sending the booking, and has to backtrack live to figure out phone vs. in-person — a procedural fragility right at the button-up stage.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be normal system latency (the CRM auto-generates before the rep specifies channel) rather than rep unpreparedness — but the rep's own phrasing ('I actually don't know') signals it as a personal gap in the moment, not a system delay being explained.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to determine appointment channel (phone vs in-person) BEFORE triggering the booking system, so the button-up sounds confident rather than improvised.

quote: Alright. So we got you for the twentieth at 1PM.
stewart_read: A specific day and time are locked, which is a genuine structural win, but the button-up skips the 'is that fair?' handshake and the no-driving/computer instruction is garbled ('the only thing they ask because you're able to access your email, and you're not driving') rather than clearly stated.
coaching_implication: Have the rep practice the button-up script verbatim for the no-driving/computer line and the fairness handshake — both are currently present in fragments but not delivered cleanly enough to anchor expectations.
